content:
Carlos Alcaraz closed out a perfect week in Vienna on Sunday, beating Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open. The Spanish star did not drop a set all week, navigating past Karen Khachanov, Nikoloz Basilashvili, Tommy Paul and Daniil Medvedev before the final. It was the 23-year-old's 28th career title and his fourth of the year, and it kept his record at the ATP 500 level this season perfect at 16-0, including titles in Doha and Tokyo. His ATP 500 winning streak now stands at 26 matches.

In Basel, Valentin Vacherot captured his second ATP title with a comeback win over Jiri Lehecka, 2-6, 6-3, 6-3. The Monegasque, who won the Shanghai Masters as a qualifier in October 2025, beat Rafael Jodar, Holger Rune and Taylor Fritz on his way to the final, and the title lifts him four spots to No. 27 in Monday's rankings.

On the women's side, Diana Shnaider returned to a career-high world No. 11 after winning in Tokyo. She led Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 4-0 in the final before Fernandez forced a deciding set, but Shnaider regrouped to win 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 for her sixth WTA title. In Guangzhou, Britain's Harriet Dart went from qualifying all the way to her first WTA title, saving three match points in a semifinal win over Sun Xinran before beating rising star Lilli Tagger 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in the final.

The season's final Masters 1000 event is already underway in Paris. On Monday, Lorenzo Musetti needed four match points in a tense second-set tiebreak to beat Hubert Hurkacz 7-6 (3), 7-6 (10) for his first win in Paris since 2022, setting up a meeting with Alexander Zverev in Zverev's first tournament as world No. 1. Ignacio Buse became the first Peruvian to win a match in Paris, beating Zizou Bergs 6-2, 6-4 to earn a meeting with Daniil Medvedev, and Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata routed Luciano Darderi 6-2, 6-2 to set up a match against Novak Djokovic or Basel champion Vacherot.

Meanwhile, Venus Williams lost her 17th consecutive singles match on Monday at the Hong Kong Tennis Open, falling 6-2, 6-3 in the first round to fellow American Mary Stoiana in 77 minutes. The 46-year-old, a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, said after the match that her future plans are up in the air.

Sources: Roland-Garros.com; Tennis Majors; Field Level Media.

excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open without dropping a set, Valentin Vacherot won in Basel, Diana Shnaider won in Tokyo and Harriet Dart claimed her first WTA title in Guangzhou, as the Rolex Paris Masters got underway Monday.
title: Tennis Weekend Roundup: Alcaraz Wins Vienna Without Dropping a Set, Vacherot Takes Basel, Shnaider and Dart Win WTA Titles
